methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); automaker signals

pit_profile.why: Ford Motor Company 'designs, manufactures, markets, and services a full line of connected, increasingly electrified passenger and commercial vehicles: Ford trucks, utility vehicles, vans, and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles'; among its risk factors, 'Industry sales volume in any of Ford’s key markets can be volatile and could decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, or significant geopolitical event' and 'Ford’s near-term results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States' (its own FY2021 10-K); EV is live (from about 2020) and its 10-K risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Ford

theme_watch.reason: Live: Ford's own FY2021 10-K, under 'Ford’s near-term results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States.', says 'A shift in consumer preferences away from larger, more profitable vehicles with internal combustion engines (including trucks and utilities) to battery electric or other vehicles in our portfolio that may be less profitable could result in an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations in the near term.' Its business: 'designs, manufactures, markets, and services a full line of connected, increasingly electrified passenger and commercial vehicles: Ford trucks, utility vehicles, vans, and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles'. The stock trades at 8.9x FY22E — near its own median. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (EV) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing electric-vehicle substitution of Ford's combustion-engine profits specifically.

classification.quality_note: Ford Motor Company 'designs, manufactures, markets, and services a full line of connected, increasingly electrified passenger and commercial vehicles: Ford trucks, utility vehicles, vans, and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles'; among its risk factors, 'Industry sales volume in any of Ford’s key markets can be volatile and could decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, or significant geopolitical event' and 'Ford’s near-term results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States' (its own FY2021 10-K); EV is live (from about 2020) and its 10-K risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Ford. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price fair; Ratio B 1.65x; +48% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.05; conservative 2yr +15%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -69.0%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +10.3%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +14.0%/yr (FY12-FY21 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +53.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: F (retrospective, 2022-11-25) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.65x (92.9% downside to Bear $1 / +56.2% upside to Bull $22) | Adj composite 2.23 vs market 2.28: gap -0.05 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +48% above the EPP floor $10 (6x FY22E $1.59) | Conservative 2-yr case: +14.8% total (+7.4%/yr) | At 8.9x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $19 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; wholesale units +7.3% in Q3 2022, forward revenues +10.4% (no Q4 2022 revenue guide, Q3 2022 revenue as reported); EV is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
